A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DRL2 research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching material moved between v1 Appendix H and v2 Section 5.

before.justification: v1 reports original gridworld and simulated robotic-control experiments in Figures 4–5, together with appendix ablations and additional task evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds maze evaluations, state/reward ablations, stochasticity tests, SARSA experiments, and additional outcome measurements.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same Bayesian transition-kernel estimation, MRP value computation, potential-based shaping, and virtual-sink construction. The explicit transition-count posterior in v2 Section 3.2 clarifies the existing update. LDBA-only and Reward-shift are experimental alternatives, not changes to DRL2.

E1.justification: v2 adds a sequential maze with more atomic propositions and intersections (Appendix D), randomized initial states, and sticky-action scenarios (Appendix J). These extend the existing tabular task families and environmental conditions; the original gridworld, Fetch, Doggo, and HalfCheetah coverage remains.

E2.justification: v2 Appendix H, Figure 12 adds LDBA-only and Reward-shift comparisons against DRL2 and No exploration on easy tabular tasks. The original comparisons retain LCER, Count-based, No exploration, and the existing kernel and virtual-sink variants.

E3.justification: The additional evaluation substantially extends the experimental design: Appendix K substitutes SARSA for Q-learning, Appendix J uses uniformly sampled starting positions and sticky actions with probability 0.1, and Appendix L measures constraint-violation rates and finite-episode formula satisfaction alongside discounted returns. The original settings and Table 1 hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained sink, kernel, and prior-strength studies, v2 tests whether low-level state information and binary rewards matter (Appendix H), robustness to stochasticity (J), and dependence on off-policy learning (K). Appendix L additionally separates avoidance behavior and actual satisfaction from return improvement, substantially broadening the diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: v1 Appendix J.3 and v2 Appendix M.3 both specify means over 10 seeds, 95% simple bootstrap confidence intervals, and smoothing with kernel size 10. The new satisfaction measurement also uses bootstrap intervals across seeds; no changed run count or uncertainty-reporting practice is established.

E6.justification: The original benchmark and ablation curves are retained, while v2 Figures 8, 12, and 14–18 add substantial result sets. For example, LDBA-only remains at zero return across the tested easy tasks, and DRL2 achieves near-unit finite-episode sequential satisfaction from the earliest plotted episodes. These are additional findings under new comparisons, scenarios, or metrics, rather than improved scores on the original settings.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix H adds mathematical reasoning that nonzero rewards on undiscounted non-accepting transitions can produce divergent infinite-horizon values, motivating the binary reward restriction. Proposition 3.1 and its Appendix A proof remain unchanged. Definition 2.5 reorganizes the existing product-MDP construction rather than introducing a different one.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: Bayesian value estimation over an LDBA-derived MRP supplies informative exploration rewards, with a consistency analysis and applications from tabular to high-dimensional continuous environments. The additional evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 6 substantially expands the limitations to rare LDBA transitions, misleading symmetric priors, stochastic off-policy learning, and dependence on a correct automaton and accurate labeling function. Section 4.2 qualifies the interpretation of noisy continuous results. New appendix discussions explain reduced-state failures, reward-shift behavior, and the distinction between avoiding violations and completing a task.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents the transition-count posterior and count-based shaping formula, changes the code-access pointer from the project website to a direct GitHub repository, and expands the computational-cost and reward-scaling discussion. Existing hyperparameters, hardware requirements, and approximate runtimes are retained; these additions mainly improve documentation.

R1.justification: After accounting for the relocation of v1 Appendix H, v2 adds substantive positioning against information-directed exploration, action masking, and goal-conditioned reinforcement learning. Section 5 distinguishes task-directed rewards from information acquisition, hard action restrictions, and multi-goal value functions, with new references including Nikolov et al., Stolz et al., and Schaul et al.

P1.justification: Editorial changes are concentrated in consolidating related work into thematic parts of Section 5, expanding baseline and limitations prose, and presenting the existing product MDP as a numbered definition. Citation style and publication headers also change. The abstract, core method exposition, and overall main-section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds seven multipanel empirical figures: Figures 8, 12, and 14–18. It also adopts the TMLR typography and page layout, enlarges or relocates existing displays, and rearranges Figure 3 from stacked to horizontal panels. Earlier performance plots and Table 1 are retained rather than replaced by new numerical content.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens validation through state/reward controls, stochasticity and SARSA tests, and direct satisfaction and violation measurements, while its expanded limitations make applicability clearer. These are useful, evidence-supported gains, but the added validation remains principally tabular and supplementary; the central proof and high-dimensional performance evidence are unchanged.
